0.content:
Aisa Bathhouse (also: Aisa Sentou, Sea Duck Bathhouse): The Aisa Bathhouse is an indoor bathhouse in Inazuma City's Tenryou district, inspired by the volcanic hot springs of Natlan. It offers a spa, fine dining and, since a renovation led by Yumemizuki Mizuki, psychotherapy from yumekui-baku (dream-eating) psychologists. Samurai of the Tenryou Commission are among its regulars.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Aisa Bathhouse is open and popular. It has operated since Inazuma opened (2.0), was renovated after Natlan, and Mizuki is working on expanding the brand.

1.content:
Amakane Island (also: Amakane-jima, Sweet Gold Island): Amakane Island is a small festival island just off the western coast of Byakko Plain on Narukami Island, Inazuma. Its name means roughly "Sweet Gold Island". In the in-game description, people sit among its blooming sakura in summer to watch fireworks in the distance.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Amakane Island is unchanged: a quiet festival spot in Inazuma.

2.content:
Amakumo Peak (also: Amakumo-touge): Amakumo Peak is the fragmented, storm-wrapped heart of Seirai Island in Inazuma, a place of constant Electro tempests. Long ago the huge Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir was killed over the island and her fury was held down by wards kept at the Asase Shrine. About 500 years ago the shrine's head priestess Asase Hibiki broke those wards, and the Thunderbird's lingering regret came back as the Thunder Manifestation, which still haunts the summit.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the peak remains the stormy centre of Seirai Island; no later canon read for this entry changes it.

3.content:
Amenoma Smithy (also: Amenoma Kaji-ya, Amenoma Art): The Amenoma Smithy sits at the eastern end of Inazuma City, in Hanamizaka. Its master, Amenoma Tougo, and apprentice Hajime follow the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden. The school is known for avoiding special tricks and relying on endless practice and willpower.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the smithy continues to operate in Hanamizaka, with Tougo as owner and Hajime as apprentice. Nothing newer has been found.

4.content:
Araumi: Araumi is a promontory at the northern tip of Narukami Island in Inazuma, cut off from the rest of the island by Mt. Yougou to its south. Beneath it lie the ruins of an ancient city that runs down under the earth and the sea and was abandoned after the Cataclysm. Its sealed passages hide Electro puzzles, Ruin Sentinels and the sunken mansion of the tengu Reizenbou.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Araumi is abandoned, with no residents and no reported change since its release.

5.content:
Asase Shrine (also: Asase Jinja): The Asase Shrine is a subarea of Seirai Island in Inazuma. It was founded to manage the wards that hold down the lingering resentment of the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, felled over the island. The shrine is now looked after by Neko, a big black cat who calls herself its Provisional Head Priestess, waiting for the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki, who never came back from a great thunderstorm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine stands renovated, with Neko still waiting for Hibiki's return. Sealing the Warding Stones quieted the island's storm.

6.content:
Autake Plains (also: Autake Heigen, Plains of Autake): Autake Plains is a subarea of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.2. It was blanketed in a fog that could not be removed, and is scattered with ruins and Electro hazards.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Autake Plains is clear of fog and unchanged since 2.2.

7.content:
Bantan Sango Detective Agency (also: Bantan Sango, Sango Detective Agency, Everything Sango Detective Agency): The Bantan Sango Detective Agency is a private detective office in Hanamizaka, the suburb of Inazuma City north of the river. It is run by the detective Sango, who is its manager and president, with Ryuuji as her assistant. Its advertisement board promises to investigate anything on a client's behalf, from missing persons and pets to marital investigations, commercial commissions, procurement and delivery.

People: Sango is the detective and manager; Ryuuji is her assistant who gathers evidence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the agency is open and unchanged: Sango still runs it and Ryuuji still works for her.

key: Village of the People of the Deep
8.content:
Bourou Village (also: Village of the People of the Deep): Bourou Village is an ancient village on Watatsumi Island, the far island of Inazuma opposite Narukami. Its people are said to have come from Enkanomiya deep beneath the waves, and it became a rallying point for those opposed to the Vision Hunt Decree. The village served as a camp where the Watatsumi Army's soldiers trained during its fight against the Shogunate.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Bourou Village is calm; the army patrols as peacekeepers and the village lives on.

9.content:
Byakko Plain (also: Byakko no Ya, White Fox Plain, White Fox Plains): Byakko Plain is a low, sparsely wooded field in the southwest of Narukami Island, Inazuma. The main road from Konda Village to Inazuma City runs through its centre, and wild kitsune can be found near the city's outskirts. Its name means "White Fox Plain".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Byakko Plain is unchanged.

key: The Sacred Forest in the Moonlight
10.content:
Chinju Forest (also: Chinju no Mori, The Sacred Forest in the Moonlight): Chinju Forest is a sacred grove in a small river valley just south of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island, and the path to the Kamisato Estate runs through it. For some unknown reason it is shrouded in perpetual night, with the glow of an unseen moon. Tanuki statues, torii gates and abandoned shrines are scattered among the trees, and legend says mischievous beings play pranks on walkers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forest is unchanged: moonlit, quiet and full of tanuki statues, with Ioroi still in his stone.

11.content:
Chirai Shrine (also: Chirai Shaden): Chirai Shrine is a stretch of ruined shrine buildings on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It is one of the three places on the fog-bound island where a Perch must receive offerings in the world quest A Particularly Particular Author, and its ruins hide a door into the Tsurumi Underground Ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is ruined and populated only by monsters; the island's curse and fog were lifted in Version 2.2 and no later content changes the place.

12.content: Court of Flowing Sand: Court of Flowing Sand is a Domain of Forgery on the north side of Mt. Yougou, Narukami Island, Inazuma. Its description says that in antediluvian times, now lost to history, a foolish ruler dreamed of building a high garden in honour of the white sacred tree over the primordial sands; now a dead silence fills the kingdom built on sand, but the obsessions of the past remain.

13.content:
Dainichi Mikoshi (also: Great Sun Mikoshi, Helios, Hyperion, Byakuya no Hikari, Oohirume no Omikoshi): The Dainichi Mikoshi ("Great Sun Mikoshi") is the artificial sun of Enkanomiya, the hidden realm of Inazuma. The ancient craftsman-sage Aberaku no Mikoto made it to protect the people of Byakuyakoku from the Dragonheirs of the Depths, now called Bathysmal Vishaps. When it burns the realm is in Whitenight, and when it is dark, in Evernight; mechanisms around Enkanomiya can toggle the two. The structure and the ground around it form a subarea of the realm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Dainichi Mikoshi still serves as Enkanomiya's sun and can be toggled between Whitenight and Evernight.

14.content:
Depths of Mt. Yougou (also: Mt. Yougou: The Depths, Depths of Mount Yougou): The Depths of Mt. Yougou is the dark space beneath Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island where the central roots of the Sacred Sakura lie. Its plants have grown gnarled and unnatural in utter darkness, and something twisted was sealed there. It is opened only at the end of the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual, when the barrier is lifted and the Miasmic Tumor made of the roots' accumulated filth is destroyed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Depths are cleansed. No 6.x or 7.x story content about them was found on the wiki.

15.content:
Dragonbone Flower (also: Dragonbone Orb, Fretnaught Fruit): The Dragonbone Flower is a giant flower in the Serpent's Bowels of Enkanomiya. During the world quest Lotus Eater, the Traveler waters it with the Waters of Lethe from Tokoyo Reisen, and after a wait it condenses into a Dragonbone Orb: a fruit whose scent calms the mind and sweeps worries away. Its story is a warning that comfort can dull the will to resist.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the flower remains in Enkanomiya's Serpent's Bowels, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes its story.

16.content: End of the Oneiric Euthymia: End of the Oneiric Euthymia is a Trounce Domain on Mt. Yougou, Narukami Island, Inazuma. It is unlocked after Transient Dreams, the second act of the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest (Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter), and lets players relive the battle against Magatsu Mitake Narukami no Mikoto, called the Shogun, as a memory. Its description says dreams once blew about like petals, never fulfilled; this is the origin of Eternity, and also 'her' end.

17.content:
Enkanomiya (also: Tokoyokoku, Delphi Pytho, Palace Below the Depths): Enkanomiya is a sunken realm deep beneath Watatsumi Island in Inazuma, entered through a pool beside Sangonomiya Shrine. Once a surface nation called Delphi Pytho, it fell into the depths during the ancient war of funerary flame and became Tokoyokoku, then Byakuyakoku, lit only by an artificial sun, the Dainichi Mikoshi. The Watatsumi people descend from its inhabitants, whom the serpent god Orobashi led back to the surface. Today it is an empty ruin of ghostly Shades of Tokoyo and hostile Bathysmal Vishaps.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Enkanomiya remains an empty, sealed ruin beneath Watatsumi, visited mainly by the Traveler. Its people's descendants live on Watatsumi Island.

18.content:
Evernight Temple (also: Tokoyo Reibyou): The Evernight Temple is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the sunken ancient land reached from beneath Watatsumi Island. It is a ruined sacred site where a faintly glowing stream, the Tokoyo Reisen (once called the River Lethe), runs close by. Offerings, hidden rooms and spectral figures from old Byakuyakoku are scattered through it, among them a fragment of the dead inventor Aberaku.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple stands unchanged in Enkanomiya, explorable and empty of living people. Nothing newer than its 2.4 content was found.

19.content:
Fort Fujitou (also: Fujitou-toride, Wisteria Helmet Fort): Fort Fujitou is a Watatsumi Army camp on Yashiori Island, where soldiers of the Sangonomiya resistance, led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, held ground against the Shogunate's forces. It sits among thunderstorms and the Tatarigami-stricken land of the island. The Traveler meets the officer Kaida Ryouma and the blacksmith Miyazaki Saburou there, and a man named Kaji who starts the Orobashi's Legacy quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is still a Watatsumi Army site, though quieter, since the Vision Hunt Decree ended and soldiers moved on to peace work.

20.content:
Fort Hiraumi (also: Hiraumi Fort, Hiraumi-toride, Flat Sea Fort): Fort Hiraumi is a subarea at the eastern tip of Seirai Island, the Inazuman island scarred by a long-ago calamity and a perpetual thunderstorm. It is a fort-like site on the island, roamed by Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders and home to the Slumbering Court, a domain. The in-game map calls it Hiraumi-toride.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fort Hiraumi is an open, hostile exploration area on Seirai Island; the wiki records no change since 2.1.

21.content:
Fort Mumei (also: Mumyou-toride, Fort of Ignorance): Fort Mumei is a group of ruins on Yashiori Island, remains of an ancient, majestic city that fell in the Archon War when the serpent god Orobashi invaded the island and clashed with the Raiden Shogun's forces. It lay under the sea until the Traveler finished the Orobashi's Legacy quests, when the fort rose out of the water near Watatsumi Island.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruin stands above water and the island's Tatarigami weather has calmed with its wards repaired.

22.content:
Hanamizaka (also: Flower-Viewing Slope, Hanamizaka district): Hanamizaka is the suburb of Inazuma City on the north side of the river that cuts through the city's northern part, one of the city's three parts alongside Tenryou and Tenshukaku. It is a district of family workshops and shops: the Naganohara fireworks shop, Amenoma Smithy, Kiminami Restaurant, Yae Publishing House and the Bantan Sango detective agency. Its name means "Flower-Viewing Slope".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hanamizaka is an ordinary peaceful suburb; the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees are over and the shops are open.

23.content:
Higi Village (also: Scarlet Tree Village): Higi Village is a small village on Yashiori Island in Inazuma, whose main export was Crystal Marrow. The war between the Watatsumi Army and the Shogun's Army, and then the Tatarigami curse of the serpent god Orobashi, emptied it. Most residents fled, died or were sacrificed; the chief Washizu, once a kind man, went mad, while a boy named Chouji tries to sell Crystal Marrow to leave.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Higi Village remains largely abandoned; Washizu is dead and the curse has not been lifted.

24.content:
Inazuma (also: Nation of Eternity, Inazuma Archipelago, Land of Eternity): Inazuma is the island nation of Eternity off the far east of Teyvat, near the Dark Sea. Its god is the Electro Archon Raiden Ei, the Raiden Shogun. For centuries a deathless puppet (the Shogun) ruled in her place while her mind meditated in the Plane of Euthymia. The Shogunate governs from Inazuma City and the castle Tenshukaku on Narukami Island, with daily affairs run by the Tri-Commission. Inazuma is a land of cherry blossoms, red maples, thunderstorms, shrines, swordsmanship, and youkai living alongside humans. It was recently closed off by the Sakoku Decree, while the Vision Hunt Decree seized its people's Visions. Both decrees are now repealed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Inazuma is at peace and open. The Vision Hunt is over and the Visions have been returned, Sakoku is lifted, a ceasefire with Watatsumi holds, and Ei takes a more direct part in governing.

25.content:
Inazuma City: Inazuma City is the capital of Inazuma, built on cliffs at the southern tip of Narukami Island. Most of the nation's people live here, and it is Inazuma's liveliest and most prosperous place, known for low crime and a great many family businesses. The city rises in three parts: the suburb of Hanamizaka, the commercial streets of Tenryou, and at the top Tenshukaku, the castle where the Raiden Shogun resides and rules.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Inazuma City is peaceful and open. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished in 2.1 and the Sakoku Decree in 2.5; the Shogun still rules from Tenshukaku.

26.content:
Jakotsu Mine (also: Jakotsu Koukou, Snake Bone Mine): Jakotsu Mine is a mining area on Yashiori Island, a stormy island of Inazuma where the remains of the slain serpent god Orobashi lie. Once home to miners and their families, it was abandoned after the Tatarigami began sickening the island's people. Today it is a rain-lashed, lightning-struck site containing a broken ward, the bandit-held Formation Estate and the empty house of a boy named Chouji.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Jakotsu Mine is deserted. The storms stop once its ward is repaired in Orobashi's Legacy: Part III.

27.content:
Jinren Island (also: Jinren-jima, Blade Gang Island): Jinren Island is a cluster of broken isles at the northernmost tip of Inazuma, lying in the shadow of Mt. Yougou. The expedition description says that in a less peaceful time it crawled with deserters who fell into banditry. Kairagi and Nobushi ronin hold it in its main story.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Jinren Island is unchanged in lore; Jirou has returned home.

28.content:
Kamisato Estate (also: Kamisato Yashiki, Kamisato Residence): The Kamisato Estate is the large residence of the Kamisato Clan on Narukami Island in Inazuma, and a point of interest in the Inazuman Archon Quests. The clan head Kamisato Ayato and his younger sister Kamisato Ayaka live and work here. The Yashiro Commission, one of Inazuma's three Commissions, has its headquarters inside the main building.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the estate is the working seat of the Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission, with Ayato as head and Ayaka as the public face of the clan. No change to its position has been recorded.

29.content: Kannazuka: Kannazuka is an area of Inazuma made of rocky, cliff-ringed islands lying between Narukami Island and Yashiori Island. Its name is said to mean "the hill where no gods reside": neither the Shogun's faith nor Watatsumi's has a hold there. It holds Tatarasuna, where the Mikage Furnace (Inazuma's largest smelter) makes Jade Steel for swords. It also holds the Kujou Encampment, the Shogun's Army headquarters that faced the Watatsumi resistance during the recent civil war.

30.content:
Kiminami Restaurant (also: Kiminami Ryoutei, Kiminami's, Kiminami eatery): Kiminami Restaurant is a well-known family restaurant in Hanamizaka, the suburb of Inazuma City north of the river, owned and cooked for by Kiminami Anna. Its Japanese name marks it as a ryoutei, and its family says its cooking descends from the Shogunate's royal head chef. Locals know it for classic Inazuman dishes, unlimited lemon water and, since the Traveler's visit, a Mondstadt-style mushroom pizza on the menu.

People: Kiminami Anna owns and cooks; her mother helps her.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the restaurant is open and Anna runs it. Her father has still not come back, as far as canon says.

31.content:
Komore Teahouse (also: Komore Djaya): The Komore Teahouse is a teahouse in Inazuma City owned by the Yashiro Commission and run on a strict members-only basis. The Kamisato Clan uses it as a local base and private meeting place; only guests it approves may enter. Its boss is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu who once served as a ninja dog of the Shuumatsuban.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the teahouse remains a members-only Kamisato Clan haunt in Inazuma City, with Taroumaru as boss.

32.content:
Konda Village (also: Konda): Konda Village is a small, quiet village on Narukami Island, long the Shogunate's chief dye-producing village and famous for lavender melons and its dish Konda Cuisine. A few old families live there, led by the village chief Konda Densuke. With the Sakoku Decree and the war, trade dried up. Beneath its dry well lies a seal tied to the Sacred Sakura.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Konda is a quiet village; the well's barrier is open and the ritual is complete.

33.content:
Koseki Village (also: The Silent Fishing Village, Stone-Surmounting Village): Koseki Village is a silent, abandoned fishing village on Seirai Island in Inazuma. A calamity that created a perpetual thunderstorm at the island's heart drove its people out, and only the memory remains that it was abandoned because of furious, unchecked storms. Today it is a ruin of empty houses where Treasure Hoarders and monsters loiter.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Koseki Village remains abandoned, though the island's storm has been calmed.

34.content:
Kujou Encampment (also: Kujou Jin'ya, Kujou Camp, Shogunate camp in Kannazuka): The Kujou Encampment is the headquarters of the Shogun's Army in Kannazuka, a fortified military camp run for the Tenryou Commission. Its purpose, as the official map text puts it, is to guard against rebellion from the people of Watatsumi Island. It was the Shogunate's front line in the civil war between the Raiden Shogun's followers and the Sangonomiya resistance, and the Kujou Clan, who head the Tenryou Commission, take their name onto its banners.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp has not appeared in 5.x-7.1 content. Its last known state is the post-war period of Inazuma 2.x: a ceasefire between the Shogun's Army and the Watatsumi Army, with soldiers who expect the peace to be brittle. Masahito remains a Shogunate officer, and Kujou Kamaji heads the clan in an acting capacity.

35.content:
Kunado's Locus (also: Kunado's Land, Tower of the Three Realms, Towers of the Three Realms): Kunado's Locus is one of the three hidden corner towers of Byakuyakoku, built so that the Human realm could sit stably between the Vishap Realm and the Abyssal Void. It is concealed by secret arts, and only shrine maidens such as Eboshi and the Vassals of Watatsumi can summon it. Its trial is Kunado's Trial, guarded by a Jibashiri named Daimon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Locus is unchanged, an ancient tower that the Traveler once passed through.

36.content:
Mikage Furnace (also: Mikage Roshin, Mikage Furnace Emergency Containment Dome): The Mikage Furnace is the largest smelting facility in all the islands of Inazuma, a huge furnace at the centre of Tatarasuna in Kannazuka, ringed by jagged rock. It mass-produced Jade Steel, the metal of Inazuma-made swords, by drawing on Tatarigami energy. The war between the Shogunate and the Watatsumi Army halted production, and the plant stands sealed behind a containment dome. The Traveler helps restore it in Tatara Tales.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Mikage Furnace is running again after Tatara Tales.

37.content: Momiji-Dyed Court: Momiji-Dyed Court is a Domain of Blessing on Yashiori Island, Inazuma. It is described as a silent scene of ever-falling red leaves, where lost causes and unforgettable loves may follow the veins of the earth and coalesce into fruits of the court's white tree. Within, summer and autumn are split into two spheres, one that strengthens Cryo and one that strengthens Pyro.

38.content:
Moshiri Ceremonial Site (also: Moshiri Saijou, Tsurumi ceremonial grounds): The Moshiri Ceremonial Site is the sacred ground of the Thunderbird Civilization on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. In the world quest series Through the Mists, illusions of the island's long-dead people gather here to repeat their last ceremony for the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir, under a curse that replays the island's destruction.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the site is empty. The curse over Tsurumi Island has been lifted and the Thunderbird Civilization's spirits have moved on; nothing in later content revisits it.

39.content: Moshiri Kara: Moshiri Kara is a one-time domain on Tsurumi Island, Inazuma. Its description calls it a mansion set up somewhere outside the Sea of Fog by an unknown builder, now a den of ravenous rifthounds (monsters from the rift).

40.content:
Mouun Shrine (also: Mou'un Shrine, Mou'un Jinja, Dark Cloud Shrine): Mouun Shrine is a shrine in the west of Watatsumi Island, the Inazuman island ruled by the Sangonomiya Shrine and the Watatsumi people. It holds an Offering Pool in which, locals say, the wishes of the faithful collect and dissolve into the water, and it is the place where Tsuyuko, a Sangonomiya shrine maiden, first asks the Traveler for help in "The Moon-Bathed Deep". Its name may honour Mouun, a shrine maiden of Watatsumi legend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is open to visitors with its Statue of The Seven and Offering Pool; the wiki records no change since 2.1.

41.content:
Mt. Kanna (also: Kanna-zan, Mount Kanna, Mt Kanna): Mt. Kanna is the mountain at the heart of Tsurumi Island, a hollow cavern from which, in the account Kama gives, the great Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir would launch into the sky like a violet meteor visible even through the fog. An altar to her stands inside. It is where the Traveler finishes the Tsurumi story by fighting a Thunder Manifestation and helping the boy Ruu keep an old promise.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the fog and thunderstorm are gone and the altar's tree has leaves again; no later canon read for this entry changes this.

42.content:
Mt. Yougou (also: Yougou Mountain, Yougou-zan, Mount Yougou): Mt. Yougou (Yougou-zan) is the holy mountain of Narukami Island in Inazuma. At its peak stands the Grand Narukami Shrine, the largest shrine in Inazuma, surrounded by the huge Sacred Sakura, a tree in perpetual bloom that purifies the land and stands for the Electro Archon's eternal watch. The mountain is crossed by long stairways and torii gates, and an electrified pool lies at its base.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Grand Narukami Shrine remains the seat of the Raiden Shogun's worship in Inazuma under Yae Miko, and the Sacred Sakura stands in bloom.

43.content:
Musoujin Gorge (also: Musoujin Hazama, Rift Valley of Yashiori Island): Musoujin Gorge is a narrow, majestic rift valley in the east of Yashiori Island. It is no natural feature: legend and official texts say it is the scar left when the Electro Archon killed the great serpent god Orobashi with her sword technique, the Musou no Hitotachi, cleaving both serpent and island. Lightning still echoes in the canyon, and the Tatarigami, the lingering curse of the slain god, broods in its gloom.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the gorge remains a scarred, thunderous canyon with hostile creatures, and Orobashi is still worshipped by the people of Watatsumi.

44.content:
Naganohara Fireworks (also: Naganohara Hanabi-ya, Naganohara Fireworks Shop, Naganohara fireworks store): Naganohara Fireworks is the fireworks shop of the Naganohara Family in Hanamizaka, on the north bank of Inazuma City. NPC Takami of the Yashiro Commission calls it the oldest and one of the best fireworks shops in all of Inazuma. It is owned by the pyrotechnician Yoimiya, who learned the craft from her father Naganohara Ryuunosuke, and it organises the Naganohara Fireworks Show that lights up festivals across Inazuma.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shop is still run by Yoimiya, with her father living in Hanamizaka. The Sakoku Decree, which was in force while Takami spoke of shipping lanes, has since been lifted. No 5.x-7.1 content changes the shop.

45.content: Narukami Island: Narukami Island is the largest island of Inazuma and the heart of the Shogunate. Its coast holds Inazuma City, crowned by the castle Tenshukaku from which the Raiden Shogun rules. Ritou is the walled-off port where all foreigners enter. Above them rises Mt. Yougou, topped by the Grand Narukami Shrine and the Sacred Sakura. Inside the island are farming and dyeing villages, fox-haunted plains and moonlit sacred forests. Inazuma's public festivals and cultural events are held here.

46.content:
Nazuchi Beach (also: Nadzuchi no Hama): Nazuchi Beach is a stretch of shallow coast joining Kannazuka and Yashiori Island in Inazuma. Its name once meant "to be tenderly caressed by the hands of the gods", but the shoal has seen far too much battle. Torn flags, broken arrows, shattered masts and wrecked decks lie along it, and it has long been a haunt of scavengers, pirates and ronin. In the Archon Quest it is where the Sangonomiya Resistance faced the Shogun's Army.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the beach remains a deserted battlefield of wrecks, stragglers and scavengers, with the Vision Hunt Decree war long over.

47.content:
Oina Beach (also: Oina Kaigan): Oina Beach is a subarea on the coast of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little recorded lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna the Traveler uses a Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving here and sees part of Kanna Kapatcir's memories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the beach.

48.content:
Outlander Affairs Agency (also: Ongoku Kansatsu, Outlander Affairs Bureau, Distant Country Supervision): The Outlander Affairs Agency is the Kanjou Commission office in Ritou that handles documents and requests from visitors who are not from Inazuma. While the Sakoku Decree was in force, any outsider who wanted to stay in Ritou had to apply here for a Residence Permit and pay a "handling fee", and the agency used its position to fleece stranded foreigners. Inspector Yurika runs the counter and Chiba guards the entrance.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the agency still exists in Ritou. Yurika and Chiba were last seen at their posts after the Sakoku Decree ended, and processing has become routine. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions the agency.

49.content:
Outsider Shrine: The Outsider Shrine is a modest shrine at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island, next to a man called Washizu. He insists that people who pray there three times in a day will be rewarded by a "he" who listens, and the shrine itself shows no sign of anything unusual. It is the centre of the hidden objective Washizu's Prayers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the objective and follow-up quest are unchanged, Washizu is dead, and the shrine's prayers no longer function after completion.

50.content: Palace in a Pool: Palace in a Pool is a one-time domain beneath Suigetsu Pool on Watatsumi Island, Inazuma. Its description says that seawater once did not fill the pool and that moonlight, brighter then, flowed through it like quicksilver. It holds the ancient mansion of Umigozen, famed throughout Inazuma for a window where one could drink wine and watch the flowers; now it is empty and only bandits and thieves dwell there.

51.content:
Plane of Euthymia (also: Euthymia, Pure Land of One Mind, Isshin Joudo, Ei's inner world): The Plane of Euthymia is the inner world of Ei, the Raiden Shogun. Over 400 years ago, after building the Shogun puppet to rule in her place, Ei withdrew her consciousness into it to meditate on eternity and protect her spirit from decay. It is a space of mind, not a place one walks to, and it lies within the sword Musou Isshin kept inside the Shogun. For centuries Ei admitted no one.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Plane remains Ei's inner retreat, but she is no longer sealed in it.

52.content:
Police Station (also: Inazuma City Police Station, Bugyou-sho, Commissioner's Office): The Police Station is the Inazuma City office of the police, in the Tenryou district. Its in-game description says it is responsible for maintaining law and order in Inazuma, and the Japanese name means Commissioner's Office. It is staffed by the yoriki Owada, who just wants a quiet career, and a new doushin, Uesugi, who wants bigger cases.

People: Owada is the yoriki; Uesugi is a doushin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wiki records no change to the station: Owada and Uesugi are still listed as its staff and the notice text is the same.

53.content:
Ritou (also: Ritou Harbor, Outlying Island): Ritou is the port on Narukami Island where every non-Inazuman entering or leaving Inazuma is processed. It is under the jurisdiction of the Kanjou Commission, whose ruling Hiiragi Clan has its estate here, and it holds the Outlander Affairs Agency, the foreign merchants' International Trade Association, and a plaza shaded by a great red maple. Under the Sakoku Decree, foreigners who arrived could go no further without a hard-won Travel Permit.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Ritou is open: the Sakoku Decree was abolished in 2.5, foreigners come and go freely after processing, and the Kanjou Commission is far less corrupt under Hiiragi Chisato.

54.content:
Royal Hot Springs (also: Royal Bath, Royal Bathhouse, Go-onsen, Imperial Onsen): The Royal Hot Springs is a hot-spring bathhouse at the headquarters of the Tenryou Commission in Inazuma City, near Tenshukaku. It is reserved for the lords of the Shogunate, who are served and housed by its manager Mikawa Akane, and outsiders are not allowed in.

People: Mikawa Akane manages the springs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the springs are still reserved for Shogunate lords with Akane as manager; the wiki records no change since 2.0.

55.content:
Sacred Sakura (also: Shin'ou, Giant Thunder Sakura, Primeval Sakura, Crimson Sakura): The Sacred Sakura is the divine tree that towers over the Grand Narukami Shrine at the top of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. It stands for the Electro Archon's protection of Inazuma: its roots purify the land's ley lines and keep Abyssal corruption from invading, and the sakura blossoms across the island have all fallen from it. Because filth builds up in its roots, the Grand Narukami Shrine must perform the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual from time to time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred Sakura is cleansed and glowing. No 6.x or 7.x content altering that was found on the wiki.

56.content:
Sangonomiya Shrine (also: The Pearlescent Palace, Coral Palace): Sangonomiya Shrine, also called the Pearlescent Palace, stands at the centre of Watatsumi Island, the outermost island of Inazuma. A palace flanked by shells and sea rocks, it is the island's centre of government and religion alike: here the Divine Priestess Sangonomiya Kokomi rules, and here rest relics of Orobashi, the dead serpent god whom Watatsumi's people still worship instead of the Raiden Shogun. During the war against the Vision Hunt Decree it was the headquarters of the Watatsumi Army.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is peaceful and still Kokomi's seat. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished, peace talks with the Shogunate followed, and the Watatsumi Army now serves mainly as peacekeepers and helps rebuild.

57.content: Seirai Island: Seirai Island is a broken, storm-wracked island of Inazuma. About 1,500 years ago the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, ravaged it until the Electro Archon killed her on Amakumo Peak, and wards held back the storm her death left. About 500 years ago a shrine maiden broke those wards to help the pirate Ako Domeki rebel against the Shogunate. A huge Electro storm then engulfed the island's centre, shattered the land and drove its people away for good. Today only Asase Shrine stands intact, kept by a talking cat called Neko who still waits for her mistress to return.

58.content:
"Seiraimaru" (also: Seiraimaru, The Stranded Flagship): "Seiraimaru" is a subarea of Seirai Island named for the flagship of the bandit captain Ako Domeki, which was destroyed there. The rundown atakebune warship lies stranded among thunder-scarred terrain, its wreck still marked by what looks like starlit tears.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ship remains a wreck on Seirai Island, nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

59.content:
Serpent's Head (also: Serpent Head, Orobashi's skull): The Serpent's Head is the skull of the great serpent god Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, left on Yashiori Island where the Electro Archon killed it. The weathered bones now form a landscape of their own: a subarea of Inazuma battered by rain and thunder. The skull still gazes at the sky, but the god is dead and its name is slowly being forgotten.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Serpent's Head remains a desolate, largely deserted site; the storms cease once Orobashi's Legacy is completed.

60.content: Shakkei Pavilion (also: Tutelage: Castle of Scrolls): Shakkei Pavilion is a one-time domain in Tatarasuna, Kannazuka, Inazuma. Its description says the magnificent mansion was built by an ancient ascetic warrior in the depths of the earth, using scenery borrowed from the outside world (shakkei, a garden-design principle), and was sealed at some point for reasons unknown.

61.content:
Shirikoro Peak (also: Shirikoro-yama, Shirikoro Mountain): Shirikoro Peak is a rugged part of Tsurumi Island, the fog-shrouded island of Inazuma that once held two ancient civilisations. A great tree called a perch stands in a cave here, one of the places where the islanders once made offerings to the Thunderbird. Beneath the peak runs a stretch of underground ruins full of Electro puzzles, Seelie courts and ancient Ruin machines.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tsurumi Island's fog is gone and the curse is lifted, so the peak is a quiet ruin-filled hill.

62.content: Slumbering Court: Slumbering Court is a Domain of Blessing at Fort Hiraumi on Seirai Island, Inazuma. Its description says this great hall stood when Seirai Island had neither its present name nor the colour of thunder, and that the scenery within will probably never change. The masterless mansion has become a haunt of rifthounds.

key: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God
63.content:
Statue of the Omnipresent God (also: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God, Symbol of Eternity, Shogun's statue): The Statue of the Omnipresent God is a vast statue built in front of Tenshukaku in Inazuma City as the "Symbol of Eternity". It was raised after the Vision Hunt Decree so that every confiscated Vision could be embedded in it. Its Visions were taken away and returned to their owners after the Traveler defeated Ei in Chapter II. Its earlier English name was the Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the statue's Visions are gone: they were returned to their owners after Chapter II. The decree was repealed.

64.content:
Suigetsu Pool (also: Suigetsu-chi, Water-Moon Pool): Suigetsu Pool, the "Water-Moon Pool", is a subarea of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. A once-famous mansion belonging to the warrior Umigozen lies beneath it, and the place is covered with ancient ruins and Ruin Machines. The mansion is the setting of the one-time domain Palace in a Pool.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mansion remains abandoned; no later canon read for this entry changes it.

65.content:
Tatarasuna (also: Tatara Sands): Tatarasuna is an island in Kannazuka, Inazuma, ringed by mountainous crags with a huge blast furnace, the Mikage Furnace, at its centre. It was where Inazuma smelted its famed Jade Steel, powered by Tatarigami energy. Twice it has gone wrong: about 400 years ago in the incident remembered as the Tatarasuna Mystery, and again in the war years when the furnace's runaway power and Fatui interest in it brought the Traveler to help. Today the furnace is purified and the area is quiet.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the furnace is purified and stable since Tatara Tales, and the island is a quiet ruin of industry.

66.content:
Tenryou (also: Tenryou district, Inazuma Commercial Street, Emperor's Land): Tenryou is the commercial heart of Inazuma City, the district below Tenshukaku built around a bustling commercial street. It is one of the city's three parts, with Hanamizaka and Tenshukaku. Adventurers, shoppers, watchmen and Shogunate officials mix here, among teahouses, restaurants, craftsmen, the Adventurers' Guild and a police station.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenryou is a safe, prosperous market district; the Decrees are over.

67.content:
Tenryou Commission Headquarters (also: Tenryou-bugyou-fu, Tenryou Commission Office): The Tenryou Commission Headquarters is the seat in Inazuma City of the Tenryou Commission, the executive arm of the Shogunate. The Commission is led by the Kujou Clan and handles security and military affairs; in the Archon Quests it is the organisation that carries out the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. The building has a courtyard exterior and an interior that the story opens in Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters is still the Tenryou Commission's seat. The commissioner's post stays unsettled: Kujou Kamaji acts as head and the Kujou Clan was given more time. Many Tenryou samurai relax at the Aisa Bathhouse.

68.content:
Tenshukaku (also: Tenshu, Shogun's residence): Tenshukaku is the castle keep at the top of Inazuma City on Narukami Island, the residence of the Raiden Shogun and the place from which she rules Inazuma. Built during the Archon War, it is one of the three parts of the city alongside Hanamizaka and Tenryou, and the Tenryou Commission Headquarters stands within its grounds. The Statue of the Omnipresent God, built to hold Visions confiscated under the Vision Hunt Decree, stands before it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenshukaku remains the Raiden Shogun's residence and seat of rule. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished in 2.1, Signora died here, and Ei has since reconsidered how she rules.

key: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
69.comment: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
69.content:
The Altar at The Serpent's Heart (also: Altar at the Serpent's Heart, Serpent's Heart altar): The altar at the Serpent's Heart is a circular chamber in Enkanomiya with five blue wall panels, each tied to a different Key Sigil. In Evernight, entering a sigil pattern in the right order makes it spawn a chest, an enemy or a spirit, and two world quests start here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar stays as released in 2.4 and has no further role in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

70.content:
The Arsenal (also: Tatarasuna Arsenal): The Arsenal is a cave under Tatarasuna in Kannazuka, south of the Mikage Furnace, where the Tatarasuna workers hid a ruined blade. The Daitatara Nagamasa was forged by Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and became "Katsuragikiri Nagamasa" after he cut down his yoriki Katsuragi with it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arsenal stands unchanged as an explorable cave, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes the Tatarasuna story.

71.content:
The Emanant Skylight (also: Emanant Skylights): The Emanant Skylight names three places in Enkanomiya where a pool of ghostfish waits during Evernight. Gliding into the fish lifts the Traveler to a time tunnel that opens onto one of the three Locus subareas.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the three skylights remain tied to The Three Great Martial Trials, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes them.

72.content:
The Narrows (also: Narrows of Enkanomiya): The Narrows is a ruined subarea of Enkanomiya. In the earliest times it was squeezed between the mountain face and an area called the Roundlands, which gave it its name. Strange tectonic shifts in Byakuyakoku later dropped the Roundlands into the depths, so the Narrows widened considerably. Its ruins hide a chamber that only appears when the land shifts between Whitenight and Evernight.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Narrows are unchanged and the chamber is empty.

73.content:
The Serpent's Bowels (also: Serpent's Bowels): The Serpent's Bowels is a quiet subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. The wiki lists the Sangonomiya Shrine as its entrance. It is a damp network of caverns with silently flowing underground rivers, and no battle music plays here. It holds the giant Dragonbone Flower.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged: empty, quiet, with the flower still standing.

74.content:
The Serpent's Heart (also: Serpent's Heart, Delphi, Heart of Ouroboros): The Serpent's Heart is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. It was made with the power of Sunfire Phantasms, to guard secrets, imprison criminals and worship the great imaginary serpent Ouroboros. At its centre stands an altar regarded as the heart of that Cosmic Serpent, a sealing device for storing important objects. Its oldest name was Delphi, the Serpent's Land.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar's prize is gone and the prison is empty save for afterimages.

75.content:
Tokoyo Reisen (also: River Lethe, Waters of Lethe): Tokoyo Reisen, once known as the River Lethe, is a stream in the Evernight Temple area of Enkanomiya. Its water glows faintly in the dark. In the World Quest Lotus Eater the Traveler collects the Waters of Lethe here to grow a Dragonbone Orb, a fruit whose scent calms the mind and makes people forget their worries.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tokoyo Reisen is unchanged and still the source of the Waters of Lethe. No later story involves it.

76.content: Tsurumi Island: Tsurumi Island is a remote island of Inazuma that was long wrapped in a dense fog and avoided for years. It holds the remains of two vanished peoples. The older one was linked to Celestia and lies buried underground. The later one was a tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir. When the boy Ruu was sacrificed to her, the Thunderbird destroyed the tribe in grief and rage and cursed the island to relive its final days. The Traveler helped Ruu's spirit keep his promise to sing for her again. That lifted the curse and the fog, and the island's spirits are now passing on.

77.content:
Tsurumi Underground Ruins: The Tsurumi Underground Ruins are a network of caverns beneath Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. They link Shirikoro Peak, whose entrance is at the mountain's base under a Perch, with Chirai Shrine, whose entrance is beneath its ruins. They hold remains of the Thunderbird Civilization and of an even earlier civilization, together with murals.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are abandoned. The Thunderbird's curse was lifted in 2.2, and no later content adds to the site.

78.content:
Uyuu Restaurant (also: Uyuu-tei, Uyuu Pagoda): Uyuu Restaurant is a tavern-style restaurant on the commercial street of Tenryou in Inazuma City, owned by Okazaki Rikuto, who calls it an izakaya, with Okazaki Erika cooking and serving. A bulletin board beside the entrance carries messages from regular customers, including General Gorou. Its Japanese name Uyuu-tei is written with characters that echo a Chinese word for "nothing" or "nonexistence".

People: Okazaki Rikuto owns it; Okazaki Erika cooks and serves.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the restaurant is open under Rikuto and Erika; the board has Sakoku-era messages plus ones added after Radiant Sakura.

79.content: Violet Court: Violet Court is a Domain of Mastery in Kannazuka, Inazuma, an altar where violet sakura bloom eternal. Its description recounts that in the ancient past the mountains rose higher than the sky and the earth was larger than the dome of heaven, until the mirror shattered and the oceans arose; in these legends the court of the primeval sakura was severed from the other islands. Monsters now storm the altar.

80.content:
Vishap Research Lab (also: Bathysmal Vishap research site, Byakuyakoku research lab): The Vishap Research Lab is a hidden laboratory of ancient Byakuyakoku in Enkanomiya, where researchers studied and bred Bathysmal Vishaps (the "Dragonheirs of the Depths") under the personal direction of Watatsumi Omikami. It does not appear on the map. The Traveler can reach it through a phase gate on the small island north of the Dainichi Mikoshi and finds there the afterimage of a researcher called Michiya, who guards the experiment records.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lab is unchanged: a hidden, abandoned Enkanomiya site whose records are in the Traveler's archive. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions it. Enkanomiya itself is little known outside Inazuma.

81.content:
Wakukau Shoal (also: Wakukau-hama): Wakukau Shoal is a shoreline subarea of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna it is the first place where the Traveler uses the Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving and is drawn into a memory of Kanna Kapatcir.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the shoal.

82.content: Watatsumi Island: Watatsumi Island is the Inazuman island farthest from the capital, a lush land of giant coral and brightly coloured plants unlike anything elsewhere. The serpent god Orobashi raised it from his own coral some two thousand years ago so that his people could leave the undersea realm of Enkanomiya. Ei later killed him, but the islanders still worship him as the Watatsumi Omikami. Their Divine Priestess, Sangonomiya Kokomi, governs from Sangonomiya Shrine. Watatsumi led the armed resistance against the Vision Hunt Decree, and since the decree's repeal it has kept an uneasy ceasefire with the Shogunate.

83.content:
Yachimatahiko's Locus (also: Yachimatahiko no Chi, Yachimatahiko's Land): Yachimatahiko's Locus is a hidden subarea of Enkanomiya in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.4. It was the site of one of the three Towers of the Three Realms, built to keep harmony between the human, elemental (vishap) and abyssal realms. It appears on the map only after the world quest Erebos' Secret begins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged: the trial is complete and the tower stays hidden unless raised by Eboshi.

84.content:
Yachimatahime's Locus (also: Yachimatahime no Chi, Yachimatahime's Land): Yachimatahime's Locus is a hidden subarea of Enkanomiya in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.4. It was the site of one of the three Towers of the Three Realms, built to keep harmony between the human, elemental (vishap) and abyssal realms. It appears on the map only after the world quest Erebos' Secret begins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged: the trial is complete and the tower stays hidden unless raised by Eboshi.

85.content:
Yashiori Island (also: Yashiori-jima): Yashiori Island is a rain-lashed island in Inazuma, near Watatsumi Island. Here the serpent god Orobashi, worshipped by the people of Watatsumi, was slain by the Electro Archon's legendary Musou no Hitotachi, which split the island in two and left a canyon, Musoujin Gorge. The god's bones lie scattered across the island, and its lingering will, the Tatarigami curse, brings storms, sickness and madness. The Shogunate and the Watatsumi Army fought over it during the Vision Hunt Decree war.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is quiet but scarred. The civil war fought over it ended when the Vision Hunt Decree was revoked (2.1). The wards were repaired in Orobashi's Legacy, the storms have eased, and the Tatarigami linger.

86.content:
Yashiro Commission Headquarters (also: Yashiro Commission HQ, Sha-bugyou Headquarters, Yashiro Bugyo headquarters): The Yashiro Commission Headquarters is the working seat of the Yashiro Commission, the branch of Inazuma's Tri-Commission that manages shrines, festivals and cultural events. It occupies the main building of the Kamisato Estate in Inazuma City. The Kamisato Clan leads the Commission: Kamisato Ayato is clan head and Yashiro Commissioner, and his younger sister Kamisato Ayaka, the "Shirasagi Himegimi", is the public face loved by the people. The Traveler first meets Ayaka here, and Thoma, her attendant, is nearly always at hand.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters remains the Yashiro Commission's seat. Ayato and Ayaka are its leading figures, Thoma serves there, and the Commission has the most public goodwill of the three. No content from 5.x to 7.1 changes it.
